official.deadline_note: IE publishes no calendar deadline. Published wording: 'The application deadline for IE Awards is the program start date' and 'The deadline to apply is the start date of the program, unless otherwise specified in the award or scholarship description. Funds are allocated on a rolling basis.' Individual IE Foundation partner scholarships set their own deadlines, published per award.
official.application_cycle: Rolling — the financial aid application may be submitted once you have applied for admission and 'always before the start of the program'; reviewed round by round alongside admissions.
official.status_note: IE's financial aid pages are live and accepting applications on a rolling basis: 'Most financial aid applications are accepted and evaluated on a rolling basis' and 'Financial aid is competitive and funding is limited, so we encourage you to submit as early as possible.'
official.tuition_coverage_note: IE Awards 'may cover between 10% and 40% of tuition fees'; any award granted is applied to outstanding tuition fees and 'cannot be used to pay the place reservation fee (with the exception of some full scholarships and awards offered through partnering organizations and generous donors, which can cover up to 100% of tuition and living costs)'.
benefits: Direct Awards: 'merit-based awards are granted automatically upon admission—no separate financial aid application is required. All applicants are considered as part of the admissions process.'
IE Awards: available to candidates across all master's programs and 'may cover between 10% and 40% of tuition fees'.

IE Foundation Scholarships: 'IE Foundation partners with a range of organizations to offer these scholarships and awards opportunities', each with its own eligibility criteria, deadlines and application requirements.

'There are some full scholarship and awards opportunities available for specific programs offered through IE Foundation, partnering organizations and generous donors, which can cover up to 100% of tuition and living costs.'
IE states it awarded more than 18M€ for academic year 24/25, with 121 nationalities represented among funded master's students.
eligibility: Available to candidates across all master's programmes; the IE Award 'aims to provide financial aid to deserving students based on their merit and potential', with priority to 'those facing economic difficulties in financing their program'.
'All IE Awards require the submission of a financial aid application and are assessed based on both merit and financial need.'
'All candidates are automatically considered for merit-based direct awards during the admissions process.'

Regional awards (IE Latin America, North America, Middle East & Africa, Asia Pacific and Europe Awards) are open only to candidates 'residing in a country that is included in the specified region (listed below) at the time of application'.
'Please note that meeting the minimum eligibility criteria does not guarantee a favorable resolution.'

Named IE Foundation awards carry their own rules — e.g. Valentín Diez Morodo is 'Open to Mexican nationals residing in Mexico'; Kistefos Africa is open to nationals of Ethiopia, Ghana, Liberia, Nigeria, South Africa and Tanzania; Laidlaw Women's Leadership is 'Aimed at extraordinary women' pursuing an MBA.
requirements: Submit an online admission application for the master's programme(s) of your choice — the financial aid application cannot be opened or evaluated before you have applied for admission.
Submit the IE Financial Aid Application: 'you can select up to three scholarships and/or awards, but you can only be awarded one'.
'You will be required to submit a short essay and to attach financial documentation, such as your last three pay slips and your most recent income tax declaration (in English or in Spanish).'
'If you are not working, your parents or tutors will be required to submit their respective financial documentation.'
Where a named award requires it, upload the scholarship-specific essay or form in the 'Additional Documentation' section of the IE Financial Aid Application.
documents: Short essay describing your financial situation, how you plan to cover all costs associated with the programme, and why you are a standout candidate for each award you are applying for.
Most recent income tax declaration, in English or in Spanish.
Parents' or tutors' financial documentation where you are financially dependent or not working.
Scholarship-specific essay or downloadable form uploaded under 'Additional Documentation' for named awards (e.g. Laidlaw Women's Leadership Scholarship form).
selection_criteria: 'All financial aid options that require an application are a combination of need- and merit-based.'
Direct Awards are merit-based and decided inside the admissions process with no separate application.
'In the case that the IE Financial Aid Committee considers you a good fit for more than one, you will only be offered the support of highest value.'
'Financial aid is competitive and funding is limited, so we encourage you to submit as early as possible.'
'It usually takes one to three weeks to receive the resolution once you have submitted your financial aid application and been admitted into the program.'
coverage: Tuition fees — IE Awards 'may cover between 10% and 40% of tuition fees'.

Living costs are not covered by the general IE Awards; only certain IE Foundation partner scholarships include them (Kistefos Africa and Norway 'may include living expenses'; Valentín Diez Morodo 'may cover up to 100% of tuition costs plus living expenses').
No travel, installation or insurance component is published anywhere on IE's master's financial aid pages.

Published per-award values: IE Forté MBA Award 'Several awards ranging from 10,000€ to 25,000€ of the cost of tuition'; IE Northwestern University Award 'Several awards that cover between 10% and 30% of the tuition fee'; Laidlaw Women's Leadership Scholarship 'Covers between 50% and 100% of tuition fees'.
Any award granted is credited against outstanding tuition fees, not paid out to the student.
application_method: Apply for admission to the master's programme of your choice.
Log into the online financial aid platform at my.ie.edu/applymasfaid 'using the same email and password used for your online admission application'.
Select up to three scholarships and/or awards, then complete the application, upload all documentation and press SUBMIT; 'You will receive confirmation of submission on the platform.'
Once submitted and admitted, IE verifies the file is complete and 'You may be asked to submit further information and/or documentation.'

'A decision by the IE Financial Aid Committee will be made quickly... the whole process of review and outcome usually takes 1-3 weeks' and 'You will receive the decision via email, which will include the terms and conditions.'
To secure the aid, 'you will need to finish your enrollment process in the program'.
official.application_route: Apply for admission to an IE master's programme first, then submit the IE Financial Aid Application in the online platform with the same login; Direct Awards need no application at all.
official.study_mode: Full-time master's programmes (the IE Collaboration Award is 'open to candidates for all full-time master's programs'; IE separately references part-time master's students seeking employer or FUNDAE support).
official.citizenship_residency: IE Awards are open to candidates across all master's programmes regardless of nationality. Five regional IE Awards (Latin America, North America, Middle East & Africa, Asia Pacific, Europe) require the candidate to reside in a listed country at the time of application. IE Foundation partner scholarships add their own rules: Mexican nationals residing in Mexico (Valentín Diez Morodo), Norwegian citizens or permanent residents (Kistefos Norway), nationals of six African countries (Kistefos Africa), women (Laidlaw, Forté MBA, Women's, Women in Finance, Women in STEM awards).
official.international_eligibility: Yes — IE describes awarding 'more than 18M€ for academic year 24/25' across '121 nationalities represented', and IE Awards plus Direct Awards are open to candidates across all master's programmes and regions, with regional and partner awards adding nationality or residency restrictions.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No subject restriction for the generic IE Award or Direct Awards. Named awards are field- or sector-specific: IE Technology & Innovation (STEM/business/social sciences background plus at least one year of relevant professional experience), IE Entrepreneurship, IE Humanities, IE Women in Finance, IE Women in STEM, IE Collaboration (full-time master's programmes), IE Forté MBA Award (women, MBA programmes) and IE Northwestern University Award (IE Law School / Northwestern Pritzker dual programme).
official.duration: One admission cycle; awards are not transferable between programmes or intakes — 'You will be required to submit a new financial aid application for the new program and/or intake.'
official.description: IE University frames the scheme as financial aid 'to support remarkable incoming master's students from all backgrounds that may be facing economic barriers', reporting more than 18M€ awarded for academic year 24/25 across 121 nationalities. It runs as three tracks: automatic merit-based Direct Awards decided inside admissions, IE Awards covering 10-40% of tuition and assessed on merit plus financial need, and partner-funded IE Foundation Scholarships with award-specific criteria. Most awards are partial tuition reductions rather than full funding.
official.region: Spain — IE master's programmes in Madrid and Segovia (IE's own living-cost guidance covers both cities); catalogue region: Europe.
official.program_type: Institutional tuition-fee awards (Direct Awards and IE Awards) plus IE Foundation partner scholarships for incoming master's and MBA students.

verification.notes: Read IE's own Master's Awards and Scholarships, How to Apply, FAQ, scholarships list and loans pages on 2026-10-10; every coverage figure is IE's published wording (10-40% of tuition for IE Awards, 10,000€-25,000€ for the Forté MBA Award), no single euro value, cadence or calendar deadline is published for the umbrella scheme, and no English test score or MOI rule appears on any financial aid page.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat IE's master's funding as a tuition discount you have to compete for, not a stipend: Direct Awards arrive automatically with your admission offer, while IE Awards need a separate financial aid application that is not even looked at until you are admitted. Because the deadline is nominally the programme start date but funds are finite and allocated on a rolling basis, filing early in your admission round is the main lever you control. You may name up to three awards, but IE pays only one, so it will keep whichever is worth most and quietly drop the rest. The 10-40% ceiling on IE Awards means you must still budget for the majority of tuition plus Madrid or Segovia living costs.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Applicants to an IE master's or MBA who can evidence both academic/professional strength and financial need — especially women targeting the MBA or finance/STEM awards, candidates from the Europe, Latin America, North America, Middle East & Africa and Asia Pacific regional pools, and tech, entrepreneurship or humanities profiles.
application_readiness_checklist: File the admission application first; the financial aid platform only recognises you once an admission application exists.
Log into my.ie.edu/applymasfaid with the exact email and password used for admission so the two files link automatically.
Draft the essay around three published prompts: your financial situation, how you will cover all programme costs, and why you fit each award by name.
Collect last three pay slips and the most recent income tax declaration, and translate them into English or Spanish yourself rather than submitting another language.
If you are financially dependent or between jobs, brief your parents or tutors early — their documents gate the whole review and a missing link stalls the file.
Screen the scholarship-list page for awards matching your nationality, country of residence, gender and field, then pick up to three rather than defaulting to the generic IE Award.
Complete enrolment as soon as the decision email arrives; the award is only secured once you finish enrolment.
common_rejection_risks: Assuming the financial aid file is read before admission — IE states your application will not be evaluated until you are admitted, so a strong aid file cannot rescue a weak application.
Filing late in the round because the deadline is the start date, by which point the limited pot has already been committed.
Financial documents in a language other than English or Spanish, leaving the committee unable to verify need.
A tutor or parent who never submits their documentation, which leaves the application permanently incomplete and unreviewed.
Counting on stacking several awards: IE offers only the single highest-value one, so a smaller award upstream displaces the ones you were banking on.
Treating an award as cash and using it against the place reservation fee, which IE explicitly excludes.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The place reservation fee and the non-waivable 150€ application fee, 60-90% of tuition above the 10-40% IE Award ceiling, Madrid or Segovia living costs, and any payment-plan costs (a one-time non-refundable 400€ administrative fee applies when instalments run beyond three consecutive months). IE does not publish a euro living-cost figure on its financial aid pages — it points applicants to its Student Services living-in-Madrid guidance instead — so build your budget from the programme's own tuition page plus that guidance.
document_audit: The income tax declaration must be the most recent one and in English or Spanish; older returns or untranslated scans break the need assessment.
Three consecutive pay slips are expected — unemployed applicants must substitute their parents' or tutors' documentation rather than leaving the section blank.
Named awards need their own essay or downloadable form uploaded in the 'Additional Documentation' section of the platform, not emailed to financialaid@ie.edu.
Everything is submitted inside the financial aid platform; email contact with the aid office is for questions, not for filing documents.
If you later change programme or intake, the award does not travel with you and a fresh application and document set are required.
alerts: The published deadline is the programme start date, but funding is allocated on a rolling basis against a limited pot — treat rolling as now, not as later.
Awards are not transferable between programmes or intakes; a deferral or programme switch restarts the competition with no guarantee of the same outcome.
You cannot apply for financial aid once the programme has started, under any circumstances.
The committee will not revisit an award unless you can demonstrate significant and unexpected changes to your finances, and only up to the programme start date.
The 150€ application fee is never waived, and no aid can be applied to the place reservation fee.
Direct Award recipients can still apply for additional financial aid, so a smaller automatic offer does not disqualify you.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission application first, then log into the financial aid platform with the same credentials, nominate up to three awards, submit the essay and financial documents, and only then does IE verify the file and decide — normally within one to three weeks of admission.
